gitCommitNote: This is the source tree commit (Phase 3.8.7.1's own commit) the Phase 3.8.7.2 rebuild was performed against, before Phase 3.8.7.2's own commit (which adds this manifest update) exists. Phase 3.8.7.2 fixes a real, evidence-confirmed defect the operator's real Windows report surfaced after a model was successfully installed: Whisper inference was running synchronously on cpal's real-time audio capture thread, causing app slowness, degraded transcription, and intermittent UI status stalls. See docs/phase-3-8-7-2-real-time-speech-performance.md.

speechWorkerDecouplingProof.summary: The operator's real Windows report (after Phase 3.8.7.1's model installed successfully) showed app slowness, poor/repetitive transcription, empty Intelligence Feed, and intermittent NO SIGNAL. Root-caused (see docs/phase-3-8-7-2-audit.md) to Whisper inference running synchronously on cpal's real-time audio capture callback thread, blocking both real-time audio servicing and the speech_engine mutex the UI's own 3-second status poll also needed.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.fix: handle_audio_chunk moved off the audio callback thread onto a dedicated speech worker thread (mirroring the already-proven acoustic-worker pattern), fed via an unbounded channel so the real-time audio callback never blocks or drops a chunk.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.directBinaryProof: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings against the extracted cip-desktop.exe finds the mangled symbol for cip_desktop_lib::commands::spawn_speech_worker - direct proof this fix is genuinely compiled into this exact binary, not just present in source.
speechWorkerDecouplingProof.sermonContentCrossDomainFinding: Confirmed, separately, that Sermon/Content/Cross-Domain Intelligence are not wired to the live audio path at all - a pre-existing, already-documented architectural boundary (Phase 3.8's own ServiceReplay screen exists for this reason), not a regression and not fixed this phase.

runtimeDependencyProof.peImportInspection: x86_64-w64-mingw32-objdump -p against the built cip-desktop.exe lists libstdc++-6.dll as a genuine dynamic import, alongside only standard Windows system DLLs (KERNEL32, user32, ole32, etc.) and WebView2Loader.dll (already handled by Tauri's own NSIS generation). objdump run again against libstdc++-6.dll itself shows it further depends on libgcc_s_seh-1.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll, and objdump against those two shows no further non-system dependencies - the complete, closed set is exactly these three DLLs.
runtimeDependencyProof.installerExtractionProof: The packaged NSIS installer was extracted directly with 7z and inspected: libstdc++-6.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll, and libwinpthread-1.dll are all present at the installer root (the same directory cip-desktop.exe installs into, $INSTDIR - confirmed via the generated installer.nsi's `File` directives, placed after `SetOutPath $INSTDIR` alongside cip-desktop.exe and WebView2Loader.dll, with matching `Delete` entries in the uninstaller section). This is now an automated, build-time-enforced check inside scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh, not a one-off manual verification.
runtimeDependencyProof.dllSourceAndArchitecture: All three DLLs were resolved from the exact posix-threads mingw-w64-x86-64 toolchain used to build cip-desktop.exe itself (via `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++/gcc -print-file-name=<dll>`, never a hardcoded path), confirmed PE32+ x86-64 via file(1), and had debug symbols stripped (x86_64-w64-mingw32-strip --strip-debug) to keep the installer size reasonable (libstdc++-6.dll: 26.3MB -> 4.6MB) without altering their code or export tables. See pilot-evidence/3.8.6.1/build/runtime-dll-evidence.json for full SHA-256 checksums and per-DLL detail.

provenance.builtDuring: Phase 3.8.6 (Windows Whisper Build & Packaging Audit) - the operator's Phase 3.8.5 real-Windows re-test confirmed audio capture now genuinely works (SIGNAL CAPTURED, correct listening lifecycle) but isolated the remaining blocker to transcription itself ('SPEECH ERROR'). The audit (docs/phase-3-8-6-audit.md) confirmed the root cause the operator suspected: no Windows build in this project's history has ever been compiled with the `whisper` Cargo feature, so no prior installer could ever transcribe regardless of hardware. Compiling with --features whisper for this exact cross-compilation target (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, from Linux) hit two independent, real, verified toolchain/upstream defects that had to be fixed before a working build was even possible: (1) whisper.cpp's vendored `ggml` CMake build unconditionally strips the 'lib' prefix from its own static library output for any Windows target (assuming MSVC naming), but the actual linker here is MinGW's GNU ld, which requires the Unix 'libX.a' convention for a plain -lX flag - so ggml.a/ggml-base.a/ggml-cpu.a were built but never found; (2) this container's default x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc/g++ alternative is the win32-threading-model variant, but whisper.cpp/ggml link against pthread and expect POSIX threading, producing 'undefined reference to __mingwthr_key_dtor' at final link - fixed by switching to the already-installed posix-threads alternative via update-alternatives. Neither fix touches the vendored whisper-rs-sys/ggml/whisper.cpp source; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact, repeatable two-pass build process and docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md for full root-cause evidence. Separately, the audit also found and fixed a real, previously-undocumented defect that would have blocked correct transcription even with the feature/model both present: `integrations/audio` delivers AudioChunks at the capture device's own native sample rate and never resamples (by design - see its module docs), but WhisperSpeechEngine hardcoded a 16kHz assumption and the one consumer that needed to convert (handle_audio_chunk) never did - so a real Windows device negotiating 44.1kHz/48kHz (the norm for consumer WASAPI devices like Stereo Mix/Microphone Array) would have fed audio to Whisper at roughly 3x the wrong rate. Fixed by adding SpeechEngine::required_sample_rate_hz() (a new default trait method, Some(16_000) only for WhisperSpeechEngine) and a linear-interpolation resampler at the one call site that needs it. Also fixed: the real underlying model-load/inference error text (already computed by WhisperSpeechEngine and SpeechEngineError, but discarded after logging) is now retained in AppState and surfaced through the existing get_pilot_diagnostics command/System Diagnostics panel (feature compiled, model loaded, chunks received, last chunk sample rate, inferences attempted/succeeded, real last-error text) instead of the generic 'SPEECH ERROR' notice alone.
provenance.buildEnvironment: cross-compiled from Linux using rustup target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, gcc-mingw-w64 (posix-threads alternative - see whisperFeatureProof above), cmake, and nsis (makensis) via `npx tauri build --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --features whisper` after the two build.rs-external fixes described above; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact repeatable process

provenance.phase3871Update: The operator installed the Phase 3.8.6.1 artifact on real Windows hardware and confirmed it launches correctly (no DLL error, UI/audio all work) but Whisper transcription itself still failed. Phase 3.8.7's diagnostics collection isolated the exact root cause: 'Whisper model: Not found', 'Model loaded: NO', 'Speech engine ready: NO' - the whisper feature and audio pipeline are both genuinely working; there is simply no model file installed. Phase 3.8.7 also found and fixed two real, previously-undiscovered defects while investigating: (1) build.rs's git-commit embed had no rerun-if-changed tracking, so a build with no other apps/desktop/src-tauri file changed (like 3.8.6.1's own rebuild) silently kept a stale commit hash - fixed by watching .git/HEAD and its resolved ref, plus a new build_dirty flag; (2) handle_audio_chunk counted every audio chunk as an 'inference attempted' even when the speech engine was not ready, producing a misleading '60,684 attempted / 0 succeeded' reading and writing a redundant timeline row per chunk for a static, unchanging condition - fixed by checking speech.is_ready() first and short-circuiting with a new chunks_skipped_engine_not_ready counter instead.

releaseCandidateStatement: This is the Phase 3.8.7.2 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (Real-Time Speech Performance Fix) - the first Windows installer in this project's history where Whisper inference no longer runs on the real-time audio capture thread, on top of the model-provisioning feature (Phase 3.8.7.1), the DLL-bundling fix (Phase 3.8.6.1), and the whisper-feature build (Phase 3.8.6), all still verified working in this exact artifact. It is a real, verifiable build artifact - not a placeholder, not a simulation, not a fabrication - and every claim in this manifest is backed by direct inspection of this exact packaged .exe, including the compiled-in spawn_speech_worker symbol (see speechWorkerDecouplingProof, modelProvisioningProof, runtimeDependencyProof, whisperFeatureProof above). See docs/phase-3-8-7-2-real-time-speech-performance.md for the full breakdown and final gate.
modelPackagingStatement: NO Whisper model file is bundled with this installer, and none could be obtained to bundle: this container's egress policy blocks the standard model host (huggingface.co - re-confirmed fresh this phase via a live network test, HTTP 403 policy denial, not a transient failure), and no ggml/gguf model file exists anywhere in this repository to embed even if bundling logic were added. This phase adds a real alternative that does not require this container to have model-host access: an in-app 'Select Existing Model File' button (native file picker + install_whisper_model command) that validates a candidate file by actually loading it as a real Whisper model before installing it atomically - the operator downloads the canonical file themselves (their own Windows machine's internet access, not this container's) and installs it with one click, no path-typing or manual file-copying required. No automatic download and no network dependency were added to the SHIPPED APPLICATION itself - the app never initiates any network request; the operator's own separate download, on their own machine, remains the source of the file. See modelProvisioningProof and pilot-evidence/3.8.7.1/build/model-provisioning-evidence.json for the full reasoning on why an in-app automatic downloader was not implemented this phase.
physicalHardwareStatement: CONFIRMED on real Windows hardware by the operator for the Phase 3.8.7.1 artifact (packaging, launch, DLL resolution, model installation via the picker, and genuine transcription activity - the operator's own real report driving this phase). This exact THIS artifact (SHA-256 e9fd4d2d...) - the speech-worker-decoupling rebuild - has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware. It has been verified at Environment A only: full regression suite green (Rust default/whisper features, frontend unchanged), the packaged installer directly extracted and inspected (DLLs still present, whisper feature symbols present, file-picker plugin symbols present, and - directly proving this phase's fix - the spawn_speech_worker symbol compiled into the binary). The decisive next step remains the operator's own real-hardware re-test: with a real model installed and Stereo Mix selected, does CIP stay responsive while listening, does the input level stay stable (no more intermittent NO SIGNAL), does transcription produce meaningfully better (not necessarily perfect) text than before, and does Bible Intelligence actually find real scripture references when one is spoken?
githubReleaseStatus: NOT CONFIGURED - no .github/workflows directory exists in this repository, and no GitHub Release has been created for this artifact. This installer is available only via this repository's working tree (release/windows/), not via GitHub Releases or any CI/CD pipeline.
obtainingWithoutDeveloperTooling: The file at release/windows/Church Intelligence Platform_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe can be copied/transferred directly (e.g. via a git clone of this repository, a direct file download, or a USB drive) to the target Windows machine and run there. Running the installer on Windows requires none of: Claude Code, Rust, Cargo, Node.js, npm, or the CIP source tree - only the .exe file itself. A real Whisper model file (see modelPackagingStatement) must be placed separately by the operator for transcription to work.
knownLimitations: UNSIGNED release candidate - Windows SmartScreen will show an 'unknown publisher' warning on first run

This exact rebuilt artifact has NOT yet been installed or launched on real Windows hardware - Environment A (automated build-time verification, including a compiled-in symbol check for the fix itself) only. The operator's own real-hardware re-test of listening responsiveness and transcript quality is the decisive, pending gate - see physicalHardwareStatement.

Sermon/Content/Cross-Domain Intelligence are NOT wired to the live audio path - only Bible Intelligence and (separately) acoustic Music recognition are. This is a pre-existing, already-documented architectural boundary (Phase 3.8's own ServiceReplay screen exists for this reason), confirmed again this phase but deliberately NOT changed - a much larger design decision than this phase's performance fix.

This phase's fix addresses WHERE Whisper inference runs, not transcription accuracy itself - whisper.cpp's tiny.en model quality, real background noise, and Stereo Mix audio characteristics are unchanged. Transcript quality should improve (clean, uninterrupted audio reaching Whisper) but 'meaningfully better,' not 'perfect,' is the honest bar for the operator's next real-hardware test.

NO Whisper model file is bundled - the operator must download one themselves and install it via the 'Select Existing Model File' button (Phase 3.8.7.1), or place it manually at the documented path. This container cannot bundle or auto-download one - see modelPackagingStatement.

In-app automatic model download (Option B from the operator's own spec) remains unimplemented - this container cannot reach the model host to build or verify a download-and-checksum-verify path end-to-end.
Environment B (Xvfb GUI reproduction) remains unavailable in this session's container (pre-existing, isolated as a container limitation in Phase 3.8.5, not this phase's regression)

The two Windows/whisper build fixes from Phase 3.8.6 (ggml lib-naming, mingw threading-model alternative) plus the Phase 3.8.6.1 DLL-bundling fix are all container/toolchain-level workarounds, not source patches - see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh; a future container rebuild or a whisper-rs/whisper.cpp/mingw-w64 version upgrade could change whether any of them are still needed

Music Library is legitimately empty in a production build - no licensed production song dataset exists in this repository; Service Replay's default flow does not exercise Music Intelligence for this reason

The ground-up visual/UX redesign described aspirationally in the original Phase 3.8 spec was deliberately not attempted this phase either - scope remained limited to the real, evidence-confirmed performance defect
